Daily Briefings · Friday, November 13, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Friday, Nov 13, 2026

Putin refused to compromise on territory or peacekeepers in his meeting with Witkoff and Kushner, but the U.S. says Europeans will join the next round and a record POW swap is agreed; Senate Republicans are weighing a narrower defense-only reconciliation bill to close the $350B FY27 gap; SpaceX is set to attempt the first double catch of Starship today, while ULA's Vulcan return-to-flight slipped to Saturday.

← NewerLatestAll briefingsOlder →Thu, Nov 12, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: Putin told the U.S. envoys he won't soften his territorial demands and won't accept foreign peacekeepers. Even so, Washington and Kyiv say Europeans will sit at the table for the next round, and a record prisoner exchange has been agreed. In Congress, Senate Republicans are looking at a defense-only party-line spending bill to cover Trump's $350B ask for the military. In launches, Starship Flight 15 goes for the first-ever catch of both stages today, while ULA scrubbed Vulcan's return to flight with 40 Amazon Leo satellites until Saturday.

NATO

  • At the European Political Community summit in Dublin, Rutte said European allies and Canada are spending a quarter-trillion extra on defence across 2025–26 but must still do more on industrial output and Ukraine's winter needs. He said security guarantees for Ukraine are "basically done," with a U.S. "clear backstop" and Türkiye among the countries playing a role, and what's missing now is a ceasefire. (Anadolu)
  • Military Committee chair Adm. Cavo Dragone visited Budapest to discuss Eastern Flank security and hybrid threats with Hungary's new defence and foreign ministers. He also visited NATO's multinational battlegroup in Hungary. (NATO)
  • NATO sent attendees of its NATO Edge 26 industry conference in İzmir a suggestion to use the Russian-owned Yandex Go taxi app, then withdrew it after warnings about FSB access to ride data. (The Record)
  • The UK will buy three Norwegian P1118 mine-hunting "motherships" for £90M under the Lunna House agreement. London says they will support anti-submarine warfare on NATO's northern flank, and the first ship is due in 2031. (Breaking Defense)

European Union

  • 40 EPC states, including Ukraine and the UK, signed a Dublin "Declaration on key principles of European security." It says peace in Ukraine must be decided with Ukraine and that matters affecting European security must be decided with Europeans. (Élysée)
  • With Europe now promised a seat at the Russia talks, the open question is who represents the EU. Ireland's foreign minister hopes today's European Council settles it. Macron said there is "no more US support" for Ukraine and that Europeans will decide their own security. (RTÉ)
  • Ireland and Ukraine are exploring drone co-production and a possible memorandum, with Dublin eyeing maritime security. Irish ministers say the talks are at an early stage. (BBC)
  • Defence and Space Commissioner Kubilius warned SpaceX that Starlink service to Ukraine is "contracted," "not a gift," and paid for by member states. He said IRIS² will give Europe Starlink-comparable capability by 2029. (Delfi / ELTA)
  • Belgium will buy 14 Thales GM200 MM/C radars for its new "Blue Dome" air-defence network, paired with Kongsberg fire control and AMRAAMs. The network will plug into NATO integrated air and missile defence from 2027. (The Defense Post)

United States

  • Senate Republicans, with Trump's blessing, are considering a defense-only reconciliation bill to deliver the $350B he wants to replenish the military after nine months of war with Iran. They are under time pressure because their margin narrows on Dec. 15. (Semafor)
  • SDA awarded SpaceX a $9.9M study (options up to ~$12.7M) on linking its Tracking Layer missile-warning satellites to SpaceX "Plaser" optical terminals on the Space Data Network Backbone. The study addresses an optical-standard mismatch that matters for Golden Dome. (Breaking Defense)
  • Space Systems Command picked Anduril, Booz Allen and Peerless for a three-month, ~$10M competitive prototyping phase of SEWOL, a cloud-native command-and-control system for space electromagnetic warfare. One of them will be chosen to build the operational system. (ExecutiveGov)
  • A Falcon 9 launched the classified USSF-627 mission from Vandenberg on Nov. 11, its second Space Force mission in six days and the Falcon 9's 15th national-security flight of 2026. Experts suspect both missions carried Starshield satellites. (Space.com)
  • A Hegseth memo seeks to raise the Pentagon's special-operations civilian chief (ASD-SOLIC) to a service-secretary-equivalent "under secretary of strategic services." That needs Congress, but it moves 100 staff and $45M a year to the office now. (Breaking Defense)
  • AeroVironment won a $405M order from an unnamed Middle Eastern customer for LOCUST X3 counter-drone laser weapons, plus an in-country sustainment depot. (The Defense Post)
  • SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 is set to launch today at 2:45 p.m. PT from Starbase with 26 Starlink V3 satellites. It will try to catch both Super Heavy and, about 22 hours later, the Ship, which would be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket. (Space.com)
  • ULA scrubbed Vulcan's return to flight (Amazon Leo LV-01, 40 satellites) and reset it for Saturday at 9:32 a.m. PT. The flight debuts a redesigned solid-booster nozzle and retrofitted BE-4s, and the Space Force wants to see the data before it lifts its pause on national-security Vulcan launches. (Spaceflight Now)
  • Blue Origin will not bid in NASA's commercial space station competition, stepping back from Orbital Reef. (SpaceNews)

European space

  • Kubilius's "Launch Tour" reached Rome on Nov. 12, feeding a 2027 Commission Action Plan on European Access to Space. Italy pushed for more Ariane/Vega flights and a bigger IRIS² role but kept its reservations about the EU Space Act's scope and licensing. (The European Post)
  • OHB repeated its opposition to the planned Airbus–Leonardo–Thales space merger and said it is confident EU regulators will weigh the threat to competition. (Space Intel Report)

Global space & defense

  • In a televised Kremlin meeting with Witkoff and Kushner, Putin rejected "grey zones" and foreign peacekeepers and held to his annexation claims, while offering a short local ceasefire. Zelensky said new Starshield restrictions are hampering Ukraine's interception of Russian jet drones. (Dawn / AFP)
  • After meeting the envoys in Dublin, Zelensky and Kushner said Europeans will join the next trilateral round ("We cannot conclude this deal without Europeans," Kushner said). Zelensky hailed an agreed exchange he called the biggest POW swap of the war. (DW)
  • China launched the "Pathfinder" technology-demonstration satellite from Jiuquan for its "Origins" space-science program, testing technologies for future missions like Hongmeng and Kuafu-2. (CGTN)
  • China's Tianwen-4 Jupiter mission will include a lander targeting Callisto, according to a new call for payloads. (SpaceNews)
